task: Corneal transparency: the Maurice lattice / destructive-interference mechanism -- compute the fraction of light scattered vs fibril spatial-disorder/structure factor; show destructive interference among short-range-ordered scatterers suppresses scattering below the independent-scatterer prediction, matching measured >90%-ish visible transmittance; falsify via (a) randomizing fibril positions must predict a large scattering rise, (b) swelling/edema must show a quantified transmittance drop, (c) an independent-scatterer adversary ignoring interference must over-predict scattering against measured transmittance.
confidence_tier: literature-parameter-anchored geometric/optical model (verified X-ray-diffraction fibril geometry + Gladstone-Dale refractive indices + directly measured human corneal transmittance spectra), NOT a reprocessing of primary EM/X-ray raw coordinate data (unavailable for live fetch this session). The scattering computation is a closed-form paracrystal (Debye-Waller) structure factor + Rayleigh-Gans-Debye cylinder model with ONE calibrated overall constant (see gates); ratio/falsifier conclusions are prefactor-independent.

benedek_1971_master_theory.numbers: VERBATIM (full abstract): 'we provide a mathematical demonstration of the Bragg reflection principle ... namely, that the scattering of light is produced only by those fluctuations whose fourier components have a wavelength equal to or larger than one half the wavelength of light in the medium ... We demonstrate physically and quantitatively that a limited correlation in the position of near neighbor collagen fibers leads to corneal transparency. Next, the theory is extended to predict the turbidity of swollen, pathologic corneas, wherein the normal distribution of collagen fibers is disturbed by the presence of numerous lakes-regions where collagen is absent. A quantitative expression for the turbidity of the swollen cornea is given in terms of the size and density of such lakes.' MASTER THEORY PAPER -- this doc's closed-form S(q)=1-exp(-q^2 sigma^2) derivation is an independent re-derivation of the same Bragg-reflection mechanism described here.

symmetric_qc_open_items: RGD cylinder scattering prefactor is CALIBRATED (one degree of freedom) against the mean of two real decorrelated measurements at 550nm, not independently re-derived from a verified textbook constant this session -- disclosed. Ratio/falsifier conclusions (G2, G3) are prefactor-independent by construction; absolute T(lambda) away from the calibration point is a model extrapolation.

Human-specific fibril diameter/spacing point-estimate not separately re-extracted from a human-only live source this session -- used Meek & Leonard 1993's verified CROSS-SPECIES range (human included among the 4 species) and picked a mid-range value (a=14nm), cross-checked via the independent G6 over-determination rather than a human-only point measurement.

The task's own pre-registered falsifier threshold ('>90% across 400-700nm') is not strictly met by the REAL measured spectrum either (Beems & van Best 1990: 80% at 450nm) -- reported honestly (G1/G1b) rather than forcing a calibration to paper over the mismatch.

Lakes/edema simulation (exploratory, void-carving on the same paracrystal base, R_lake=300nm as an undisclosed-provenance model parameter) is directional-only -- it shares the finite-simulation-patch limitation diagnosed for the order/disorder brute-force cross-check (Orient, section 3 of the doc). A monotonic scattering increase with lake fraction was observed but its magnitude is not quantitatively trusted; not included in the final gated results.

A genuine, disclosed finite-size numerical artifact was found and diagnosed via a perfect-lattice-alone control (S(q) should be exactly 0 away from Bragg peaks for a perfect finite lattice as N->infinity, but stayed O(0.01-0.2) across a 16x range of simulated N without a clear shrinking trend) -- this is why the analytic closed-form result, not the brute-force direct-summation simulation, is used for all quantitative gate claims. Brute-force agreement was good (7.9% median error) only in the large-disorder regime where the artifact is negligible.

5 of 16 citations are pre-abstract-era PubMed records (title/PMID/DOI/PMCID verified live, no abstract text available for independent re-extraction this session): Maurice 1957, Hart & Farrell 1969, Freund et al 1986, Hedbys & Mishima 1966, Goldman et al 1968. Raw EM/X-ray coordinate data was not reprocessed this session (not available for live fetch in this sandboxed environment) -- the geometric model uses literature-reported summary statistics, not a re-analysis of primary micrographs. Freund et al 1995's interference-factor number IS a raw-EM-image analysis, but it is THEIR result, correctly cited, not reproduced here.
